attributes.title: Level 2

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you update the counter variable name in the expressions of the inner for loop?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What should the counter variable be named in the inner for loop, so that it can be used to set the Box sprite’s y-position?


Solution: 

x should be replaced with y in all 3 expressions of the for loop
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code!


Notice that the error message on the bottom says that the problem is on Line 88: the program cannot find the name ‘y’.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the y variable is used as the counter in the for loop that sets the Box sprite’s y-position.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ Did you add the yOffset variable to the Box sprite’s y value so that the Box sprites do not appear too high on the screen?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which variable offsets the Box sprite’s y-position?


Solution: 

+ yOffset should be added to the end of the box.y code on Line 88.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the Box sprites appear too high on the screen! 


Fix the bugs in the code so that the Box sprite’s y values are offset from the edge of the screen.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ Did you update the Player sprite’s z-position to a value greater than 0 so that it appears in front of the Box sprites?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which property sets the depth of the Player sprite on the screen?


Solution: 

monkey.z value should be changed to a value larger than 0.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the Player sprite appears behind the Box sprites!


Fix the bugs in the code so the Player sprite appears in front of the Box sprites.

subgroups.name: solve 4

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the correct operator to change the value of the boxesOpened variable so that the variable increases by 1?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which operator always increases a variable’s value by 1?


Solution: 

+ should be changed to an increment operator ++ so the code reads: boxesOpened++ on Line 99.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code!


Fix the bugs in the code so that when the Player sprite overlaps with a Box sprite and the A button is pressed, the boxesOpened variable increases by 1.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 2 of Purple Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about for loops. Using for loops, you can code things to happen multiple times. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 2:

badges.title: Getting Loopy
badges.description: Control how a loop runs using its 3 expressions in JavaScript.

badges.title: Here We Go Again
badges.description: Write a for loop that starts at zero and counts up using an increment operator.

badges.title: Where it Stops, Nobody Knows
badges.description: Write a for loop that runs a random number of times.

badges.title: Sugar, We’re Going Down
badges.description: Write a for loop that starts with a number larger than zero and counts down using a decrement operator.

badges.title: Double the Fun
badges.description: Nest a for loop inside another for loop.

badges.title: Memory Palace
badges.description: Save the game’s high score.

badges.title: Trophy Room
badges.description: Display the high score to the user.

badges.title: Depth Perception
badges.description: Set a sprite’s z-position so it appears in the front of a scene.
